key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin pairs weld-pool simulation with Gaussian-process surrogates to screen robotic welding conditions and control strategies for future in-space metal joining.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could support welding-parameter adjustment as robot travel speed changes, reducing reliance on costly flight-like testing during early development.
method: Finite-volume thermal model includes phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure; gravity is assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates are compared using repeated five-fold cross-validation.
A simulated six-axis UR5 follows an L-shaped seam while proportional control adjusts the power-source setting.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs; 74/80 held-out solver responses fell within nominal 90% predictive intervals, and finite-volume checks placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative root-side-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-only; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop tests are needed to assess model and controller validity.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
